title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 55-57): in this fourth draft of 'Analysis situs', Grothendieck is building a combinatorial, 'tame' model of spaces. A space is encoded by:
- a lattice F of 'figures' (or 'fragments'), ordered by ≤;
- a subset M of 'elementary' figures (cells). Every figure is a Sup of elementary ones.
- operations on figures: interior c̊, 'support' or closure |c|, and product ×.
He is trying to define the right notion of morphism f: F → F'.

Previous page:
1°) f should be monotone and preserve arbitrary Sup. Then f is determined by its restriction f_M: M → F'.
2°) f should preserve Inf. For finite Inf this reduces to the formula f_M(X) ∩ f_M(Y) = Sup_{Z∈X∩Y} f_M(Z), which he compares to the covering identity X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k} X_k. For infinite Inf one reduces to decreasing filtered families.
In modern terms, f is a frame-type map (arbitrary joins, finite meets) on a lattice generated by join-irreducibles, determined by its values on the generators, as in Birkhoff/Alexandrov duality.

This page:
(i) He doubts that commutation with infinite Inf need be part of the definition.
(ii) He wants f_M also to be compatible with c̊ and |c|; compatibility with × is already known. But this only makes sense once one decides what it means when f_M sends elementary figures not to elementary figures of M' but to arbitrary figures in F'.
(iii) Before that, he proposes a stronger condition (**), comparing p. 28: for every figure F, with F' = f(F), the map C ↦ f(C) from the ordered set of subfigures of F to the subfigures of F' is an isomorphism of ordered sets.
Modern reading: f restricted to each lower set (closed star / closure of a cell) is an order isomorphism onto the corresponding lower set of the image. That is, a 'locally isomorphic', discrete-fibration-like, dimension-preserving cellular map.
(iv) He notes that (**) forces elementary to go to elementary, i.e. f_M: M → M'. This is exactly the issue he was pondering: are there natural 'homomorphisms' not sending M into M' that he would want to admit? Example B on p. 50 is one, but he finds it heterogeneous and unappealing 'for reasons of dimension'.
(v) A struck-out passage tried to restate (**) as a condition (**_M) on elementary figures.
Next page: he settles on f_M = f: M → M' as on pp. 27-28. He observes that such f behaves 'almost like an embedding', since it is an isomorphism on each normalized figure, but need not be injective.

The problem served: choosing the category of morphisms for his combinatorial spaces, cellular maps that do not lower dimension versus general continuous-type maps.
errors: No mathematical error. The page is deliberative: it does not decide whether infinite-Inf commutation is required, and gives no definition of compatibility with c̊, |c| for maps that do not send M into M' (an acknowledged gap, resolved next page by restricting to f: M → M').

ideas.what: Morphisms of figure-lattices as maps preserving arbitrary Sup and finite Inf, determined by their restriction to elementary (join-irreducible) figures
ideas.modern_name: Frame/locale homomorphisms; Birkhoff-type duality for lattices generated by join-irreducibles; morphisms of Alexandrov spaces / face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937); Alexandrov (1937); locale theory (Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone)

ideas.what: Condition (**): f induces an order isomorphism from subfigures of F onto subfigures of f(F), forcing cells to map to cells
ideas.modern_name: Dimension-preserving (non-degenerate) cellular maps; maps of face posets that are isomorphisms on lower intervals, i.e. discrete fibrations / 'combinatorial étale' maps of regular CW posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in combinatorial topology (CW posets: Björner 1984; poset coverings)

ideas.what: Observation that such maps are 'almost embeddings' (isomorphic on each closed cell) yet not injective
ideas.modern_name: Cellular local isomorphisms / combinatorial coverings or immersions

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open the right notion of morphism for his combinatorial 'analysis situs' allowing cells to map to non-elementary figures (non-cellular maps), set aside 'for reasons of dimension'. The broader tame-topology/analysis-situs program of these 1986 notes is little studied, but this particular design choice is standard.
missed.quote: si je connais des "homomorphismes", que j'admettrais aussi d'appeler, et qui n'appliquent pas M dans M'! Oui, il y a exemple B p. 50, mais dans ce cas il m'apparaît hétéroclite
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents his choice of dimension-preserving, locally-isomorphic cellular maps as morphisms in his combinatorial model of tame spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine design deliberation about which maps between lattices of cells to admit. The ideas (join-preserving maps determined on generators; maps that are isomorphisms on closed cells) are standard combinatorial and lattice-theoretic notions. Mildly interesting only as a window into the unpublished 1986 analysis situs project.
transcription_corrections: 'f_U', 'U', 'U'' should probably read 'f_M', 'M', 'M'' (script M, set of elementary figures), consistent with the previous and next pages.
'Ss f_o(F)' is likely 'Ssfig(F)' (set of subfigures of F), cf. 'Fig(M)' on the next page.
'en plus de ≤, à c̊, |c|': the operations are c̊ and |c| (interior and support/closure).
The last lines read approximately: 'il y a exemple B p. 50, mais dans ce cas il m'apparaît hétéroclite et peu engageant pour des raisons de dimension (**)'.
'65' at the bottom left is the archive foliation number, not part of the text.
